Summary of Changes (2026 Rules of Tennis)

rulesetReview.currentText: Points are called love (0), 15, 30, 40 and game. At 40–40 (deuce), a player must win two consecutive points: advantage, then game.
rulesetReview.note: Matches standard ITF Rule 5 as generally known; the alternative No-Ad method (deciding point at deuce, receiver chooses side in singles) is in an appendix. search snippet only; source not opened

rulesetReview.currentText: A set is won by the first player to win six games with a margin of two. At 6–6 a tie-break is normally played: first to 7 points with a 2-point margin.
rulesetReview.note: Rule 6 allows both 'advantage sets' (no tie-break) and 'tie-break sets'; the organiser chooses. Wording is broadly right but should mention advantage sets. search snippet only; source not opened

rulesetReview.currentText: Matches are best of three or best of five sets. Some events replace the final set with a match tie-break (first to 10 points, win by 2).
rulesetReview.section: Appendix VI per 2025 amendments snippet (not opened)
rulesetReview.note: Snippets of ITF 2025 amendments: an appendix (moved to Appendix VI per snippet) allows a 10-point tie-break at 6-6 in the final set (as used at Grand Slams), and the match tie-break remains an alternative method. Suggest adding the final-set 10-point tie-break at 6-6. search snippet only; source not opened

rulesetReview.currentText: The server stands behind the baseline, between the centre mark and the sideline, and serves diagonally into the opposite service box. Two attempts are allowed; two faults lose the point (double fault).
rulesetReview.section: Rules 16-21; Rule 18 Case 1 (2026 amendment, per snippet)
rulesetReview.note: Generally consistent. 2026 amendment (snippet) clarifies Rule 18 Case 1: in doubles the server may stand behind the baseline between the singles and doubles sidelines; in singles not. Suggest specifying singles vs doubles sideline. search snippet only; source not opened

rulesetReview.currentText: A serve that touches the net and then lands in the correct service box is a let and is replayed.
rulesetReview.note: Correct as a description of a service let (Rule 22) per secondary snippets; note No-Let is an alternative method in an appendix, and Rule 23 covers general lets (whole point replayed). search snippet only; source not opened

rulesetReview.currentText: The server may not touch the baseline or the court inside it with either foot before hitting the ball.
rulesetReview.note: Incomplete per snippet of Rule 18: during the service motion the server also may not change position by walking/running (slight foot movements allowed), or touch the area outside the imaginary extension of the sideline or the imaginary extension of the centre mark. Suggested correction pending verification. search snippet only; source not opened

rulesetReview.currentText: The server alternates between the right and left halves of the court each point, starting from the right. Players change ends after the first, third and every following odd game of each set; in a tie-break, every six points.
rulesetReview.note: Rule 10 as quoted by tennis.com matches; add that if a set ends on an even total, players change at the end of the first game of the next set. search snippet only; source not opened

rulesetReview.currentText: A ball that touches any part of a line is in.
rulesetReview.note: Consistent with standard rule that lines are part of the court they bound; not verified. search snippet only; source not opened

rulesetReview.currentText: A player loses the point if the ball bounces twice before they hit it, they hit it out or into the net, they touch the net or the opponent's court while the ball is in play, or the ball touches them.
rulesetReview.note: Snippet of Rule 24(g) confirms the player, racket or anything worn/carried touching net, posts, cord, strap or opponent's court loses the point; suggest including racket/clothing. Full list not verified. search snippet only; source not opened

newRulePoints.text: UNVERIFIED (snippet of 2026 amendments): if players are found to be at the wrong ends during a tie-break, the error is corrected immediately and a fault served before discovery does not stand (Rule 27).
UNVERIFIED (snippet): from 2026 Rule 18 Case 1 clarifies a doubles server may stand behind the baseline between the singles and doubles sidelines; a singles server may not.
UNVERIFIED (snippet of 2025 amendments): an appendix permits a 10-point tie-break (2-point margin) at 6-6 in the deciding set, the format used at Grand Slams.

UNVERIFIED (snippet): since 2012 ITF rules require 10-and-under competition to use slower red, orange or green balls on appropriately sized courts; yellow balls are not permitted. Court sizes in Appendix (check current numbering).

UNVERIFIED: ITF appendices list alternative methods such as No-Ad scoring, short sets (first to 4 games, tie-break at 4-all) and the match tie-break (first to 10, win by 2). Exact appendix numbers for 2026 not confirmed.

claims.statement: Systematic review (Pluim et al. 2006) reported most tennis injuries occur in the lower limb, then upper limb, then trunk, with wide variation in reported incidence.
claims.section: search snippet only; source not opened

claims.statement: The same 2006 review found no randomised controlled trials of injury-prevention measures in tennis, so prevention advice (e.g. for tennis elbow) rests on low-level evidence.
claims.section: search snippet only; source not opened

claims.statement: Per a tennis.com rules column, touching the centre-mark extension at the start of the service motion is a foot fault even if the foot moves off before contact.
claims.section: search snippet only; source not opened

claims.statement: A 7-6 or 6-3 set has an odd number of games, so players change ends straight after it; the tie-break itself does not change this logic.
claims.section: search snippet only; source not opened

claims.statement: ITF Play and Stay: red, orange and green balls on smaller courts help young beginners rally and serve sooner; red-court dimensions quoted by ITF ~10.97-12.8 m x 4.88-6.1 m.
claims.section: search snippet only; source not opened

safetyReview.currentText: Clear balls from the court to avoid rolling an ankle.
safetyReview.section: not opened; lower-limb injuries most common per snippet

safetyReview.currentText: Use sun protection and hydrate outdoors.
Tennis elbow: build forearm strength, use correct technique and a racket/string setup suited to you.
safetyReview.section: not opened; snippet notes lack of RCT evidence for prevention measures

safetyReview.currentText: Shoulder: strengthen the rotator cuff and upper back; build serve volume gradually.
Warm up with mini-tennis before full rallies.
